consensus_summary: Chaff primarily symbolizes the wicked, ungodly, or worthless people separated from the righteous and destroyed (blown away or burned) in judgment, drawn from the winnowing metaphor.
book_summary: The empty wicked husk separated from the grain, driven away, and burned; unlike tares, chaff is what remains after the grain has matured.
consensus_core_identification: the wicked/ungodly as worthless residue under divine judgment
book_core_identification: the empty wicked husk (post-maturation residue) separated, driven away, and burned
boundary_disagreement: Book explicitly distinguishes chaff from tares as the husk left after grain matures, whereas consensus alternatives sometimes blend or associate the image with the wheat-tares parable for nominal believers in the mixed church.
rationale: Minimum cores are the same referent (wicked as the worthless separated residue judged via winnowing, anchored in Ps 1:4 and Matt 3:12). Book preserves that category exactly while adding agricultural precision that reclassifies boundary cases away from tares-style applications common in consensus alternatives; this is refinement of extension/precision, not replacement of the central identification.
strongest_objection: The tares distinction could be read as implying a stricter post-maturity condition that quietly narrows some ecclesial applications the consensus still tolerates as extensions.
